elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (b): "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Initial Development Activities will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner."; note the scope is limited to Initial Development Activities rather than all Development/services performed by Harpoon.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (a): "any software and other deliverables provided by Harpoon to AbbVie hereunder, including the Final Development Report, will conform in all material respects to their documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "ninety (90) days following delivery", not twelve (12) months; drafter expressly took the fallback duration.
Services (Initial Development Activities) warranty runs only "thirty (30) days following performance".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Harpoon shall, at AbbVie's election, repair or replace the non-conforming deliverable, re-perform the non-conforming activities..."
"...or refund the amounts paid for them." (subject to the non-refundable-payments tension noted below).

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Section 3.8.4 is a mutual performance covenant ("Each Party shall perform ... in compliance with all Applicable Law"), not a warranty, and carries no warranty remedy; the inserted clause adds no compliance-with-laws warranty, and Article 10 reps are given only "as of the Effective Date".

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears in the inserted clause or in the cited Article 10 provisions; drafter expressly declined this element.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "for ninety (90) days following delivery, any software and other deliverables provided by Harpoon ... will conform in all material respects to their documentation" — meets the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Initial Development Activities will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" — meets the 30-day floor for the services actually performed by Harpoon under the Initial Development Plan.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "repair or replace the non-conforming deliverable, re-perform the non-conforming activities" — express repair/replace remedy.
"or refund the amounts paid for them" — express refund remedy stated in operative language.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the inserted "Performance Warranty" supplies a 90-day software/deliverable conformance warranty, a 30-day services (Initial Development Activities) warranty, and repair/replace, re-performance and refund remedies — all four fallback elements are in operative text, not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred is not met: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty. This is a correct 'deviation' finding pitched at fallback.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise clause, nothing existing is deleted or paraphrased, and Section 10.5 is correctly left untouched because it already carves out "THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN". No survival tail, expense allocation, notice procedure or extra damages categories were added.

Intent defect to repair: the drafter's own analysis records that payments under this Agreement are expressed as non-refundable. The new remedy "refund the amounts paid for them" therefore sits against a retained contradictory sentence and may be read as inoperative. Repair by opening the remedy sentence with "Notwithstanding any provision of this Agreement stating that payments are non-refundable," (citing the specific payment section).

Two drafting points the reviewer should expect Harpoon to contest, neither fatal to minimality: (i) remedy choice is placed "at AbbVie's election" whereas the playbook model language puts it at Vendor's option — keep it, but be ready to trade; (ii) "including the Final Development Report" is an illustrative inclusion that is not required by any selected element and can be dropped if it draws fire.

Optional scope tightening: the services leg is anchored to "Initial Development Activities" only. If Harpoon performs other Development activities or services under the Agreement (e.g. Manufacturing support), consider "the Initial Development Activities and any other Development activities performed by Harpoon hereunder" so the warranty is not under-inclusive.
